title: How Does a Protein Fold? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
An earphone wire curls into a spring, then knots into a ball. Diya asks: does a protein fold like this? And why would its shape matter?

We see what structure means to a chemist, a physicist and a biologist, zoom from a red blood cell to haemoglobin to one subunit, and watch one chain fold level by level: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary. Then we read a primary structure from the N-terminal to the C-terminal, compare tertiary and quaternary structure, see why proteins have only right-handed helices with a pause and think, work through naming the level in three pictures, the haemoglobin exam trap, an original NEET pattern match question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 72 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 The earphone wire
0:35 What does structure mean?
0:54 Zoom ladder: red blood cell, haemoglobin, subunit
1:17 Four levels of protein structure
2:04 Reading a primary structure
2:29 Tertiary vs quaternary
2:47 Right-handed helices + pause and think
3:17 Worked example: name the level
3:40 Exam trap: haemoglobin subunits
4:00 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:24 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Enzymes: How They Work. A tiny pocket in a folded protein can speed up a reaction ten million times. How?
